chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) it was said: Abdullah ibn Jabala narrated to them from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding the Muslim husband and the Jewish or Christian wife, he said: 'They do not inherit from each other.'

key_terms.يَتَوَارَثَانِ: They inherit from each other (dual form)

ai.seo_question: Do a Muslim husband and a Christian wife inherit from each other in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ruling of *al-khalw* (mutual inheritance) between a Muslim man and a *Kitabiyyah* (Jewess or Christianess), establishing that they do not inherit from each other due to the disparity in religious status. While the Quranic prohibition on marrying polytheists (2:221) is often cited, this narration specifically addresses the legal consequence of that difference in the context of inheritance law, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding mixed-faith families.
